title: Split process-lifecycle code out of drain.rs to get under limits
summary: Restructure crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, which is at 1798 production lines with 5 landings in a week against a limit of 1500. Move the pid-file, PidGuard, stop/restart and RealLifecycle section (around lines 3412 to the end) into a new child module, drain/lifecycle.rs. Re-export every public item from drain so callers in main.rs and display.rs compile unchanged. The audience is the code-health gate and the maintainers. There is no behavior change.

defaults_applied.how: One focused module split, with no behavior edits.
Existing tests must pass, and clippy and fmt must be clean.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
The check is that the file is under the limit and behavior is unchanged, not that code was moved.
The file is split by responsibility rather than trimmed to just under the limit.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (item outline), crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs and crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs (callers through the drain:: path). Callers use drain::guarded, RealProcs, StopWait, PidRecord, DrainState, StopOutcome, RestartOutcome and reinstall_note. The drain.rs outline shows about 17 lines of imports plus doc comments at the top (up to line 260), then types, the Drain engine, drain_with, and from about line 3412 a self-contained process-lifecycle section: pid_file, log_file, PidRecord, Procs/RealProcs, DrainState, PidGuard, guarded, StopWait, stop_and_wait, restart, RealLifecycle. No records or data files are added, so the record validation allow-list is not involved.

Code survey: the move target is crates/athena-cli/src/drain/lifecycle.rs, a child module of drain.rs. It is declared with `mod lifecycle; pub use lifecycle::*;` (or explicit re-exports), so existing paths such as crate::drain::DrainState keep working. The producer keeps the tests with the code they test, or leaves them in drain.rs if they need private items, and may widen visibility to pub(super) where required.

The lifecycle section is chosen because it has the least coupling to the Drain engine. If the section turns out to be under 300 production lines, the producer also moves another cohesive group, for example the study_*/model_contradictions helpers or the PrLander code. The target is below 1500 production lines in drain.rs, with no function over 200 lines.
No refusal rule is added or tightened, so no newly-refused-reading percentage applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs has fewer than 1500 production lines (test modules excluded), and a new crates/athena-cli/src/drain/lifecycle.rs holds the moved code. Check with `ls` and by reading both files.

The diff only moves code, re-exports it and adjusts visibility or imports. No function bodies change in logic, and public paths such as crate::drain::guarded, DrainState, StopOutcome and RestartOutcome are still exported from drain. Check with `git diff`.
`cargo test -p athena-cli` passes, with the same tests present as before the change and none deleted or ignored. This is the outcome check: the drain behavior is unchanged.
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
`cargo build` succeeds for the whole workspace, so main.rs and display.rs callers compile without edits.

out_of_scope: Any behavior change or refactor of the drain engine logic
Changes to athena.toml code-health limits or other governance files
Splitting other files such as display.rs or main.rs
